source_title: Best Red Wines for Summer: 5 You Need in Your Rotation
newsletter_intro: Who said red wine has to go into hiding when the weather warms up? Not me. There’s a whole world of summer reds that are light, juicy, and totally fridge-friendly — and I’m breaking down five that deserve a spot in your rotation.

instagram_reel.hook: Red wine is not banned in summer. Let’s fix that.
instagram_reel.script:
Somebody told you red wine is only for cold weather? Respectfully, no. There are plenty of reds that are perfect when it’s warm out.

Think lighter-bodied, lower tannin, and in some cases, a little chill. That means wines like Beaujolais, Pinot Noir, Lambrusco, Grenache, and Zweigelt can all absolutely earn a place in your summer rotation.

Beaujolais is juicy and fresh. Lambrusco is sparkling and super refreshing. Grenache brings soft red fruit and a little spice. And Zweigelt? That’s the conversation starter.

So if you’ve been side-eyeing red wine all summer, give these a try. Your fridge and your BBQ table will thank you.
instagram_reel.caption: Red wine does not disappear when the sun comes out. There are so many lighter, fresher reds that belong in summer. Which one are you trying first?

tiktok.hook: Red wine in summer? Yes. And I’m not budging on this.
tiktok.script:
Okay, let’s clear something up: red wine is not automatically a fall and winter thing.

If you pick the right style, red wine can be amazing in summer. Think lighter-bodied, lower tannin, and sometimes even a little chilled.

My summer red shortlist? Beaujolais, Pinot Noir, Lambrusco, Grenache, and Zweigelt.

Beaujolais is juicy. Lambrusco is sparkling and fun. Grenache brings soft fruit and spice. And Zweigelt is the one people always ask about at the BBQ.

So no, you do not need to pack away red wine until September. You just need better reds for summer.
tiktok.caption: Summer red wine is a thing. A very good thing.

linkedin.post:
A common wine myth is that red wine belongs on the shelf until sweater weather returns.

Not true.

There is a whole category of reds that are built for summer: lighter-bodied wines, lower in tannin, and in some cases, even better with a short chill before serving.

In this episode of The Wine Down, I share five summer reds that make the case beautifully: Beaujolais, Pinot Noir, Lambrusco, Grenache, and Zweigelt.

For trade, retail, and hospitality teams, this is a useful reminder that red wine doesn’t have to be framed as heavy or seasonal. There’s real room to speak to guests who want freshness, versatility, and a bottle that works with warm-weather occasions.
